hits.snippet: Jordan Bond is proof that good ideas can come from unexpected places\. For Bond, the place was Norway and the idea was a life-saving mobile phone application\. “I noticed a medical study in Norway that studied whether people survived better if citizens did CPR \(cardiopulmonary resuscitation\) versus if they didn’t, using an app,” said Bond, a senior firefighter/medic with the Newport News Fire Department the past eight years\. “I think somehow that developed into PulsePoint a few years later\. “As soon as I saw PulsePoint, I was like, that needs to come here\.” Bond pitched the app to a committee of department firefighters, then to Fire Chief R\.B\. Alley III and R\.E\. Lee, the assistant fire chief of medical services\. All approved and the NNFD announced the launch of PulsePoint in a news conference Tuesday at Fire Station No\. 3\. PulsePoint is an interactive mobile app that alerts citizens within a 400-meter radius when someone suffers a Sudden Cardiac Arrest \(SCA\) in a public place\. VIDEO: The Missoula County Office of Emergency Management, along with local first responders and hospitals, partnered to locally launch PulsePoint, a mobile app designed to facilitate life-saving care in our community\. The effort comes as this week is National CPR and AED Awareness Week\. PulsePoint alerts trained individuals of the nearby need for CPR so they can help\. The app also informs users of the nearest publicly available Automated External Defibrillators\. Partnership with PulsePoint is part of a larger initiative to increase the number of CPR-trained individuals, with a goal to train 20,000 residents in Missoula County by 2026\. A $60,000 federal grant is funding this initiative\. Agencies currently using PulsePoint include: Missoula Fire Department, Missoula Rural Fire, Frenchtown Rural Fire, East Missoula Rural Fire, Florence Fire and EMS and Condon-Swan Valley Fire Department\. #### KECI-TV NBC 13 Missoula

Published May 21, 2026 at 9:00 AM MDT In today’s KSUT Conversation, Tami Graham speaks with Fred Hutt, Executive Director of the Southwest Regional Emergency & Trauma Advisory Council, and Scot Sholes, EMC Chief at Durango Fire Protection District\. They're part of a group working to launch PulsePoint, a public notification system for cardiac emergencies, in La Plata County\. PulsePoint integrates with 911 call centers to let community members receive notifications when a cardiac emergency is occurring nearby\. Such notifications increase the chance that someone in the vicinity of an emergency has a portable, automated external defibrillator, a medical device used to treat sudden cardiac arrest\. PulsePoint is part of a wider initiative to expand on the success of Heart Safe La Plata\. It's also part of a statewide initiative to implement PulsePoint as a registry for AEDs statewide\. # Dane County hosts annual Cardiac Arrest Survivor Celebration July 27, 2026 Andrew Beckett Emergency Management MADISON, Wis\. – Cardiac arrest can strike at any time, and the chances of surviving can be greatly improved by how quickly those around you are able to act\. The importance of this early intervention, and the many people who play a role in providing that care, was on full display Friday, July 24 at Dane County’s annual Cardiac Arrest Survivor Celebration\. “Nobody survives going into cardiac arrest alone, and those recognized through this annual celebration highlight how many people are often involved in saving a life,” said Dane County Executive Melissa Agard\. “Bystanders performing CPR, the 911 call taker giving instructions, the EMS crew working on a patient in the back of an ambulance, and the doctors and nurses who provide treatment and care in the hospital; all of them are an essential part of improving the chances of survival\.” The Cardiac Arrest Survivor Celebration is an opportunity to highlight Dane County and its partners’ strong commitment to improving outcomes from sudden cardiac arrest\. # Fire torches trailer just west of Las Vegas Strip by Matthew Seeman Thu, August 13, 2026 at 8:26 AM Updated Thu, August 13, 2026 at 9:24 AM Crews respond to a trailer fire west of the Las Vegas Strip on Thursday, Aug\. 13, 2026\. \(KSNV\) LAS VEGAS \(KSNV\) — A fire completely torched a trailer just blocks east of the Las Vegas Strip Thursday morning\. Clark County firefighters could be seen mopping up the scene near Polaris and Tompkins avenues, near Tropicana Avenue and Interstate 15\. The fire was reported around 3:45 a\.m\., per the dispatch website PulsePoint\. It's unclear if any injuries were reported, what caused the fire, or if an adjacent warehouse was damaged\. News 3 has reached out to Clark County for further updates\.

# CPR Bystander app reimplemented in Eagle County to shorten the time for emergency response On average, it takes five to seven minutes for Eagle County Paramedics to arrive on the scene of an emergency, according to Starting Hearts Director of Business Development, Jackie Christiansen\. For cardiac arrest victims, brain damage starts on minute four, she said\. That’s why Eagle County Paramedics are relying on citizen bystanders for their assistance by using the app PulsePoint Respond, a program that was reimplemented this past May\. Through the app, subscribers are notified in real time when a public cardiac arrest occurs in their vicinity\. If willing to assist, the person can administer aid like CPR while waiting for a professional responder to get to the emergency\. The app also tells users of AED locations nearby\. --- --- PulsePoint Respond has been used in the area before, previously funded by Starting Hearts, according to Christiansen\. This time around, Eagle County Paramedic Services are providing funding to keep the app running\. For a population of 50,000 or less, there is an $8,000 annual fee\.
